defs_parts: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: A brief agrees the task, and a GDD is detailed enough to build and test.
Reverse starts from a game, and a draft starts from an idea.
A PX goal is what the player feels, a mechanic what the player does.
Every claim carries a tag, and a tag is a claim, not evidence.
Priority Inflation means more than forty percent of features tagged CORE.
An acceptance criterion names a quantity, a tolerance and a time box.
bookends.segment: Name The Design Term, Defend It
bookends.command: Quiz me on game design document terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use reverse, draft, game brief, PX goal, mechanic, observed, assumption, scope creep, out of scope and acceptance criterion. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is a game-making situation, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike is wrong.
